m-river.name: Mã River
m-river.summary: A roughly 400-kilometre river flowing through Vietnam and Laos to the Gulf of Tonkin, whose delta was long a centre of settlement in north-central Vietnam.

red-river-asia.name: Red River
red-river-asia.summary: A 1,149-kilometre river flowing from Yunnan in southwest China through northern Vietnam to the Gulf of Tonkin, named for the reddish silt it carries.

ng-s-n-culture.name: Đông Sơn culture
ng-s-n-culture.summary: A Bronze Age culture centered on the Red River Delta in northern Vietnam, flourishing from about 1000 BC to the first century AD, known for wet-rice farming and skilled bronze casting, including the famous Đông Sơn drums.

pandanus-amaryllifolius.name: Pandan
pandanus-amaryllifolius.summary: A tropical screwpine plant whose fragrant leaves are used for flavoring in Southeast Asian, some South Asian and Hainanese cooking.

maluku-islands.name: Maluku Islands
maluku-islands.summary: Archipelago in eastern Indonesia once called the Spice Islands, prized for nutmeg, mace and cloves found nowhere else, which drew European colonial interest in the 1500s.

dong-son-drum.name: Đông Sơn drums
dong-son-drum.summary: Bronze drums made by the Đông Sơn culture of Vietnam's Red River Delta from about 600 BCE to the 3rd century CE, used as instruments and ritual objects and traded widely across Southeast Asia.

manunggul-jar.name: Manunggul Jar
manunggul-jar.summary: A Neolithic secondary burial jar from the Tabon Caves in Palawan, Philippines, dated 890–710 BCE, considered a masterpiece of Philippine pre-colonial art.

palawan.name: Palawan
palawan.summary: The largest province of the Philippines, an archipelago stretching between Mindoro and Borneo between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.

psychopomp.name: Psychopomp
psychopomp.summary: A spirit, deity or creature in many religions whose role is to guide the newly dead to the afterlife, often depicted as birds, horses or other animals in funerary art.

baiyue.name: Baiyue
baiyue.summary: Various ethnic groups living across southern China and northern Vietnam during the 1st millennia BC and AD, known for short hair, tattoos and skilled seafaring, later assimilated into Chinese culture.

maitum-anthropomorphic-pottery.name: Maitum anthropomorphic pottery
maitum-anthropomorphic-pottery.summary: Anthropomorphic burial jars discovered in 1991 in Mindanao, Philippines, dating to the Metal Age and considered unique among Southeast Asian finds.

cotabato.name: Cotabato
cotabato.summary: A landlocked province in Mindanao, Philippines, whose capital is Kidapawan.

nanyue.name: Nanyue
nanyue.summary: An ancient kingdom founded in 204 BC by the Chinese general Zhao Tuo, covering parts of modern southern China and northern Vietnam, conquered by the Han dynasty in 111 BC.

tr-ng-sisters.name: Trưng sisters
tr-ng-sisters.summary: Lạc Việt military leaders who led a rebellion in AD 40 against Chinese Han rule and ruled for three years; Trưng Trắc was Vietnam's first female monarch, before their defeat in 43 AD.

guangxi.name: Guangxi
guangxi.summary: An autonomous region in South China bordering Vietnam, home to the largest ethnic minority population in China, chiefly the Zhuang people.

emperor-guangwu-of-han.name: Emperor Guangwu of Han
emperor-guangwu-of-han.summary: Founding emperor of China's Eastern Han dynasty (5 BC–AD 57), who reunified China by 36 CE after civil war and made Taoism the dynasty's official religion.

ma-yuan-han-dynasty.name: Ma Yuan
ma-yuan-han-dynasty.summary: Chinese general and politician of the Eastern Han dynasty, 14 BC to 49 AD, who helped Emperor Guangwu unite the empire and put down several rebellions.

zhao-tuo.name: Zhao Tuo
zhao-tuo.summary: Chinese Qin general (240–137 BC) who founded the independent kingdom of Nanyue in 204 BC and later declared himself emperor, regarded by some as founder of Vietnam's Triệu dynasty.

tri-u-dynasty.name: Triệu (Zhao) dynasty
tri-u-dynasty.summary: The ruling dynasty of the kingdom of Nanyue, spanning parts of southern China and northern Vietnam, founded in 207 BC by the Chinese general Zhao Tuo and conquered by the Han dynasty in 111 BC.

an-d-ng-v-ng.name: An Dương Vương
an-d-ng-v-ng.summary: Founding and only king of the Âu Lạc kingdom in Vietnam's Red River Delta, who united the Âu Việt and Lạc Việt peoples and died by suicide after his defeat by Nanyue forces in 179 BCE.

u-l-c.name: Âu Lạc
u-l-c.summary: An ancient polity covering parts of Guangxi and northern Vietnam, founded in 257 BCE by Thục Phán from the union of two peoples, before falling to Nanyue in 179 BCE.

v-c-nh-inscription.name: Võ Cạnh inscription
v-c-nh-inscription.summary: The oldest Sanskrit inscription found in Southeast Asia, a stone stele discovered in Vietnam in 1885, erected for a King Sri Mara around the 2nd to 4th century CE.

funan.name: Funan
funan.summary: A loose network of ancient Indianized states in what is now Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam, existing from the 1st to 7th century CE, generally considered the first known kingdom in Southeast Asia.

ch-h-n.name: Chữ Hán
ch-h-n.summary: The Chinese characters used to write Literary Chinese and Sino-Vietnamese vocabulary in Vietnam, officially used from the Han dynasty's rule until the early 20th century.

classical-chinese.name: Literary Chinese
classical-chinese.summary: The written literary form of Chinese used from the 5th century BCE and adopted across Vietnam, Korea, Japan and the Ryukyus as a shared language of scholarship and administration until the early 20th century.

khmer-script.name: Khmer script
khmer-script.summary: An abugida script for writing the Khmer language and, in Buddhist liturgy, Pali, written left to right with stacked consonant clusters and both independent and dependent vowel marks.

javanese-script.name: Javanese Script
javanese-script.summary: A traditional Indonesian abugida script developed on Java, mainly used for the Javanese language from at least the mid-16th century until gradually replaced by the Latin alphabet in the mid-20th century.

balinese-script.name: Balinese script
balinese-script.summary: An abugida writing system used on the island of Bali for Balinese, Old Javanese, Malay and Sanskrit, descended from the Brahmi script and among the most ornate Brahmic scripts of Southeast Asia.

tarumanagara.name: Tarumanagara
tarumanagara.summary: An early Indianized Sundanese kingdom in western Java whose 5th-century ruler Purnawarman produced Java's earliest known inscriptions, dated to around 358 AD.

java.name: Java
java.summary: Indonesia's most populous island, home to about 159 million people and historically the center of Hindu-Buddhist empires, Islamic sultanates and the Dutch East Indies.

sugriva.name: Sugriva
sugriva.summary: A character in the Hindu epic Ramayana, king of the vanara kingdom of Kishkindha, who aided Rama's search for his wife Sita after succeeding his brother Vali.

rama.name: Rama
rama.summary: A major deity in Hinduism worshipped as an avatar of Vishnu, considered an ideal man and the heroic protagonist of the epic Ramayana.

sita.name: Sita
sita.summary: A Hindu goddess and female protagonist of the Ramayana, consort of Rama and regarded as an avatar of the goddess Lakshmi.

ho-i-c-district.name: Hoài Đức
ho-i-c-district.summary: A rural district of Hanoi in Vietnam's Red River Delta region.

ng-dynasty.name: Ngô dynasty
ng-dynasty.summary: Semi-independent Vietnamese dynasty from 939 to 968, founded by Ngô Quyền after his 938 victory over the Chinese Southern Han at the Battle of Bạch Đằng River.

vietnam-under-chinese-rule.name: Bắc thuộc
vietnam-under-chinese-rule.summary: Term for several historical periods, from 111 BC to 939 AD and again 1407–1428, when parts of northern and central Vietnam were ruled by Chinese dynasties.

c-eo.name: Óc Eo
c-eo.summary: An archaeological site in the Mekong Delta of southern Vietnam, a busy port of the kingdom of Funan from the 2nd century BC to the 12th century AD.

maharaja.name: Maharaja
maharaja.summary: A royal title of Sanskrit origin used across the Indian subcontinent, meaning prince in medieval northern India but a king in ancient and medieval southern India, used since Vedic times by many dynasties.

champa.name: Champa
champa.summary: A collection of Cham polities along the coast of central and southern Vietnam from about the 2nd century CE until 1832, shaped from the 4th century onward by Hinduism.

xiongnu.name: Xiongnu
xiongnu.summary: A nomadic tribal confederation dominating the eastern Eurasian steppe from the 3rd century BC to the 1st century AD, founded as an empire by Modu Chanyu, eventually defeated by the Han dynasty.

shiva.name: Shiva
shiva.summary: One of the principal deities of Hinduism, worshipped as the Supreme Being in Shaivism and known as 'the Destroyer' within the Hindu trinity alongside Brahma and Vishnu.

ashoka.name: Ashoka
ashoka.summary: Emperor of the Mauryan dynasty from about 268 BCE, whose empire covered much of the Indian subcontinent; after conquering Kalinga he turned to promoting Buddhism across Asia.

kutai.name: Kutai
kutai.summary: A historical region on Borneo, now part of East Kalimantan, Indonesia, home of the Kutai Martadipura Kingdom (399–1635), the earliest Hindu kingdom in the East Indies.

kalingga-kingdom.name: Kalingga
kalingga-kingdom.summary: A 6th-century Indianized kingdom on the north coast of Central Java, one of Indonesia's earliest Hindu-Buddhist kingdoms, known in Chinese sources as Helíng.

ramayana.name: Ramayana
ramayana.summary: An ancient Sanskrit epic poem narrating the life of Rama, one of Hinduism's two major epics, with its oral origins estimated between the 8th and 4th centuries BCE.

thanh-h-a-province.name: Thanh Hóa province
thanh-h-a-province.summary: The northernmost coastal province of Vietnam's North Central Coast region, bordering Laos to the west and the Gulf of Tonkin to the east.

h-ng-b-ng-dynasty.name: Hồng Bàng period
h-ng-b-ng-dynasty.summary: Legendary ancient period in Vietnamese history, said in a 15th-century chronicle to have begun in 2879 BC when Kinh Dương Vương founded the kingdom of Xích Quỷ, later renamed Văn Lang.

sa-hu-nh-culture.name: Sa Huỳnh culture
sa-hu-nh-culture.summary: A culture of central and southern Vietnam that flourished from 1000 BC to 200 AD, likely the ancestors of the Cham people who later founded Champa.

chams.name: Cham people
chams.summary: An Austronesian people, the original inhabitants of coastal Vietnam and Cambodia, who founded the Hindu-Buddhist kingdoms of Champa from the 2nd century and became largely Muslim by the 17th century.

kang-tai.name: Kang Tai
kang-tai.summary: A Chinese traveller of the mid-third century, one of the first Chinese to document the Southeast Asian kingdom of Funan.

khmer-language.name: Khmer language
khmer-language.summary: The Austroasiatic language spoken by the Khmer people and Cambodia's official language, heavily influenced by Sanskrit and Pali through Hinduism and Buddhism during the historical Chenla and Angkor empires.

saola.name: Saola
saola.summary: A rare, critically endangered forest-dwelling bovid native to Vietnam and Laos, sometimes called the Asian unicorn, first identified in 1993 and possibly nearing extinction.

cattigara.name: Cattigara
cattigara.summary: A major port city on the Magnus Sinus described by ancient sources, possibly linked by some modern scholars to the archaeological site of Óc Eo in present-day Vietnam.

kalanay-cave.name: Sa Huynh-Kalanay Interaction Sphere
kalanay-cave.summary: An Iron Age maritime trading network linking the Philippines, Vietnam, Taiwan, Borneo and Thailand from about 400 BC to AD 1500, marked by shared pottery and ornaments called lingling-o.

lingling-o.name: Lingling-o
lingling-o.summary: A ring-shaped or double-headed pendant made mostly of jade by Late Neolithic to Iron Age Austronesian cultures, chiefly in the Philippines, dating back to around 500 BC.

h-t-nh-province.name: Hà Tĩnh
h-t-nh-province.summary: A province in Vietnam's North Central Coast region, bordering Laos and the South China Sea, grouped with neighboring Nghệ An and known for its distinct regional accent.

mindoro.name: Mindoro
mindoro.summary: The seventh largest island in the Philippines, located off southwestern Luzon, divided into Occidental and Oriental Mindoro provinces.

ng-y-n-ch-u-inscription.name: Đông Yên Châu inscription
ng-y-n-ch-u-inscription.summary: An Old Cham inscription found in 1936 near the old Champa capital of Simhapura in central Vietnam, likely from the late 4th century CE. It is the oldest surviving document of any Austronesian language and reflects both indigenous belief and Hindu influence.

tr-ki-u.name: Trà Kiệu
tr-ki-u.summary: A village in Duy Xuyên commune, Da Nang city, Vietnam.

bhadravarman-i.name: Bhadravarman I
bhadravarman-i.summary: King of Champa from 380 to 413 who moved the capital to Simhapura, built temples at Mỹ Sơn, and later disappeared after being defeated by a Chinese governor.

nha-trang.name: Nha Trang
nha-trang.summary: A ward of Khánh Hòa province, Vietnam, one of 65 new wards, communes and special zones created in a 2025 reorganization of the province.
